anomalies.observed: The 3.3V LDO output is on a net named '+3.3V' (REG1 pin 1 'OUT' / pin 2 'ADJ-SENSE', which also carries the sensor ICs), while the MCU-side rail is a *different* net named '+3V3' (MCU decoupling caps, I2C pull-ups, connectors). More seriously, the MCU supply pins are on neither: FCC2 VDD pins 11/27/50/75/100 each appear only on single-node nets 'unconnected-(FCC2-VDD-PadNN)', and NAVC2 VDD pins 19/32/48/64 on 'unconnected-(NAVC2-VDD-PadNN)'. FCC2's VBAT/VDDA/VREF+ (pins 6/21/20) are likewise unconnected.
anomalies.expected: Per the specification the 3.3 V regulator output must feed both MCUs, i.e. FCC2 and NAVC2 VDD pins should sit on the same 3.3V rail as the regulator output.

evidence.quote: 3V3 feeds both MCUs (FCC, NAVC) and all I2C sensor ICs

anomalies.impact: Neither MCU receives VDD (and the sensor/peripheral rail '+3.3V' is not tied to the MCU rail '+3V3'), so both processors are unpowered and the board cannot boot or run.

anomalies.observed: NAVC2's ground pins 18 and 63 share only the private net 'Net-(NAVC2-VSS-Pad18)' (not connected to GND), its VSSA (pin 12) is left unconnected, and VDDA (pin 13) sits only on the isolated 'VDDA_NAVC' net with C99. The NAVC also does not appear on the sensor I2C bus: net 'NET0057' (SCL) and 'NET0074' (SDA) list U11, U14, U17, U18 and U7 but no NAVC2 pin, and NAVC2 has no net in common with FCC2 (no inter-MCU UART2/I2C/GPIO link).
anomalies.expected: The navigation computer must be grounded and must be the I2C master of the sensor bus (IMU, magnetometer, barometer, temperature, GPS) and participate in the FCC<->NAVC link, per the architecture description.

evidence.quote: Navigation Computer (NAVC) — gathers IMU, magnetometer, pressure sensor and GPS receiver data

anomalies.impact: The navigation computer has no ground reference and no connection to its sensors or to the FCC, so it can neither measure the environment nor supply the navigation solution to the flight controller.
